title: Per-request cost-aware admission and deferred-execution proxy
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets intermittently hit capacity cliffs when a small number of very expensive requests (long contexts or high temperature sampling) arrive, causing unfair drops for latency-sensitive tenants and poor cost predictability. Existing admission layers are per-token or per-request rate limiters but do not account for expected compute cost.

Goal: Implement an admission/proxy layer that: (1) estimates per-request GPU cost at ingress, (2) makes admission decisions using tenant provisional throughput and credit balances, (3) offers a deferred-execution queue for non-latency-critical requests with clear SLA/timeout semantics, and (4) emits autoscaler hints for short-term burst capacity. The feature should improve tail latency for latency-sensitive lanes while smoothing cost variability and reducing costly overprovisioning.

Core idea: Compute a cheap cost estimate (based on token budget, model variant, requested sampling settings, and recent KV cache hit probability) at the request gateway. Use that estimate to map requests to three paths: immediate admit (fast lane), provisional admit (charges tenant credits and may be subject to soft preemption), and deferred-execution (deferred queue executed when headroom/credits available). Admission decisions consult per-tenant provisional throughput allocations and a global headroom pool. A reconciliation daemon periodically charges actual usage and rebalances credits; autoscaler hinting uses the rate of provisional admits + deferred backlog to request transient capacity bursts from Dedicated autoscaler service.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway produces per-request cost_estimate header and logs for all admitted requests
Latency-sensitive tenants maintain p99 generation latency within 1.5x of baseline under 3x burst traffic
Deferred queue preserves request order per-tenant and honors max defer time (configurable, default 30s)
Credit reconciliation completes within 2 minutes of execution and tenant balances are consistent
Autoscaler hint events reduce tail shedding incidents by >=35% in synthetic workload tests
implementation_steps: Design cost_estimate heuristic: model tokens * sampling_factor + kv_hit_adjustment (doc in Design PRD)
Add lightweight estimator to ingress proxy (C++) and expose X-Estimate-Cost header
Extend admission controller to consult tenant_provisional_throughput and global_headroom service
Implement deferred-execution queue as a separate executor pool with bounded concurrency and per-tenant order
Build reconciliation daemon that consumes execution records and adjusts tenant credit buckets
Emit autoscaler_hint metrics to the fleet autoscaler API (burst_score, backlog_age, provisional_rate)
Integrate feature flags and rollout knobs (percent rollout, tenant opt-in, hard vs soft preemption)
Add e2e tests, chaos tests for lost reconcilation messages, and performance bench harness
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per-service-class (target: p99 < 1.5x baseline for latency-sensitive)
percent of requests routed to deferred queue (target: <10% for tier-1 customers)
autoscaler_hint_trigger_rate and subsequent capacity_added (target: reduce shedding by >=35%)
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard: per-tenant credit balance, provisional_throughput_utilization, deferred_latency_percentiles
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime gate with default off
Canary: enable for internal test tenants and infra team (2%)
Pilot: opt-in for 3 enterprise customers with dedicated SLA monitoring
Gradual ramp: per-tenant enabling using health gates (error rate, p99 latency, reconciliation lag)
Rollback: disable feature flag and drain deferred queue with best-effort immediate execution
testing_notes: Create synthetic workload with mixed short/long requests and sampling settings to validate estimator accuracy
Inject KV cache miss/hit patterns to ensure estimator handles variance
Chaos: drop reconciliation messages and verify idempotency and eventual consistency
Load test: ensure gateway overhead <5% CPU on ingress path and estimator adds <1ms median latency
